messages:
maria: Heads-up — I saw a KV-cache hit-rate drift between our replay harness and the synthetic load generator. On the replay run TTFT p95 jumped ~2.4x during a 30m window. We need an apples-to-apples bench protocol to reason about kernel selection and batching heuristics.

ash: Ugh, seen that before. Synthetic traffic usually has more uniform prefix distribution so KV cache warms differently. Do you have the run IDs?

maria: Run IDs: replay-2026-01-23-42 and synth-2026-01-24-09. Attached logs show p95/99 and kernel selection traces. Short summary: replay had more long-tail user sessions, which kept kv shards cold intermittently.

sam: Couple quick items we should standardize for any comparison:
- identical prompt corpus (same prompt ids & seeds)
- same sequence length distribution (not just mean)
- same client-side pacing / think-time distribution
- identical model binary & kernel flags (no lazy JIT during measurement)

lee: Also ensure GPU clocks and cuDNN/cublas tuners are stable. First-run kernel autotuning and mem allocs skew latencies badly. We usually add a 5–10 minute warmup phase and discard that data.

bench-bot: deploy-log: started replay-2026-01-23-42 at 2026-01-23T14:02:11Z

maria: Agreed. I sketched a minimal bench protocol below — want feedback before I formalize into the harness: 

```
bench_protocol:
  prompts: /bench/corpora/kvcache_stress.v2.json  # fixed corpus
  seq_len_dist: from_corpus
  run_mode: replay | synthetic (explicit)
  warmup: 10m (ignored samples)
  measurement: 30m
  clients: 200 (pooled)
  think_time: pareto(alpha=1.5, min=50ms)
  batching: disabled | fixed_max_batch=32 | policy=continuous
  kv_cache_policy: global_shard | per_session (must be same)
  kernel_flags: DISABLE_KERNEL_PROFILING=true, FORCE_KERNEL_HINT=fused_gemm
  env: GPU_PWR=performance
```

maria: Key point: kv_cache_policy must be identical. Replay was per_session, synth used global_shard and that alone explains ~30–40% of goodput diff.

ash: Nice. On metric defs let's lock down:
- TTFT: time from request arrival at ingress to first token emitted by runtime (includes routing + kernel startup).
- TPOT: time per output token after first token (avg across tokens for request).
- p95/p99: computed over per-request TTFT or TPOT depending on which curve we're analyzing — specify which metric in each chart.
- QPS: requests/sec arriving at ingress.
- goodput: tokens/sec that required actual compute (i.e., exclude tokens served from prefix/KV cache hits).

sam: Emphasize goodput vs QPS. We had a bug where the load generator reported QPS but many responses were 100% prefix-cache hits, so GPU utilization was low but QPS high. For cost/perf tradeoffs we care about goodput.

lee: For kernel selection sanity: include kernel provenance in trace (which kernel variant executed per layer and batch-size). If kernel choice differs between runs, annotate charts and consider forcing kernel to compare. Example trace line:
```
KERNEL_SELECT: layer=8 batch=12 seq=128 selected=fused_gemm_sm80_v3
```

maria: On batching heuristics — continuous batching (the runtime holds a sliding window to fill batches) behaves differently with replay since user arrival patterns cause microbursts. We should add a synthetic mode that replays the observed interarrival time distribution rather than Poisson to reproduce microbursts.

ash: Add these pitfalls to the doc:
- mismatched streaming vs non-streaming modes (streaming shows TTFT shorter but TPOT higher)
- varying max_context (affects KV cache hit ratio)
- client-side retries masking transient infra errors
- transport-level pipelining (HTTP/2 multiplexing) differences

maria: I ran a quick micro-check — forcing the same kernel across runs and switching kv policy to per_session made the TTFT p95 converge (within 8%). So kernel selection interacts strongly with batching: small queues trigger small-batch kernels which are less efficient at token throughput.

sam: Can we add a small script to the harness to normalize kernel selection? e.g. set ENV FORCE_KERNEL_HINT=... then verify trace equality.

maria: Yes, will add. Also adding a per-run artifact: kernel_provenance.csv and kv_hit_map.json so we can compute goodput precisely.

lee: Measurement checklist for final SOP:
1) lock model binary + commit hash
2) set GPU performance governor + warmup
3) force kernel hint or record provenance
4) use same kv_cache_policy & shard map
5) identical prompt corpus + seq_len dist
6) identical client pacing / interarrival distribution
7) run warmup then measurement window
8) export TTFT/TPOT histograms + kernel_provenance + kv_hit_map

maria: Good. One more nuance — when we force fused kernels we saw slightly higher TTFT median (kernel init overhead) but much lower TPOT tail. For application SLAs we need both: low TTFT for interactive feel and low TPOT p95 for throughput-sensitive batch completions. We'll keep both charts.

bench-bot: artifact-upload: kernel_provenance.csv attached to replay-2026-01-23-42

ash: Action items:
- maria: author formal bench protocol doc and add to harness repo (ETA Tue)
- sam: add kernel_provenance exporter to runtime traces (ETA Wed)
- lee: prepare a synthetic interarrival generator matching replay microbursts (ETA Thu)

maria: I'll run the aligned experiments once those land and post a short report with TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99, QPS, goodput and kernel diffs.

sam: +1. If any run shows >10% divergence after alignment we open a regression bug and attach kernel_provenance + kv_hit_map.

lee: thanks team. small victory: caught a dashboard bug where goodput was computed from request tokens not compute tokens — fixing that now.

maria: Thanks. I'll upload the protocol draft to the bench repo and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:
